post.summary: Create an API key
post.description:
Returns the plaintext key exactly once, in `data.token`. It is stored only as a hash and cannot be recovered afterwards. A key authenticates as its owner, limited to the scopes and IP ranges given here.
Scopes are enforced from the request itself: safe methods need `read`, mutating methods need `write`, anything under `/openai` needs `inference`, and anything under `/agent-integrations/composio` needs `connections`. A key is also pinned to the caller's team at creation.
`connections` is NOT mintable here: it is granted automatically to a hosted OpenCompany instance, which authenticates with a short-lived audience-bound cluster token rather than a stored secret. Requesting it returns 400.

`sync` and `detached` are orthogonal: `sync` decides who waits for the HTTP response, `detached` decides whether the cycle may answer before its delegated tasks finish.

post.summary: OpenAI-compatible Custom-LLM relay for the voice agent
post.description:
Called server-to-server by the ElevenLabs agent (Custom LLM) for each turn (#5399). Instead of running inference, it relays the turn over Socket.IO to the user's desktop, runs the local agent there, and streams the reply back as OpenAI `chat.completion.chunk` SSE. Authenticated by the shared `ELEVENLABS_CONVAI_LLM_SECRET` (presented as the Custom-LLM API key), not a user JWT. The user is identified by verifying the signed token the client set via `startSession`, read from `user` / `user_id` at the top level or from `elevenlabs_extra_body` — minted at `get-signed-url` and bound to the authenticated caller, so a raw user id cannot be spoofed here.
A turn whose user message is a read-back request (the desktop pushing a deferred answer back into the live session to be spoken) is answered here from that message, without waking the desktop.

200.description: Server-sent event stream of chat.completion chunks. While the desktop turn is still running the stream emits short spoken fillers so the provider does not cancel it; they stop at the first real delta. A turn that makes no progress is closed here rather than left for the provider to fail the whole session over.

400.description: Request carries no user token in any supported field.

401.description: Missing or invalid Custom-LLM secret, or invalid user token.

post.summary: Join the tokenmaxxxing waitlist

Referral attribution is write-once at creation; an unknown `ref` is ignored rather than rejected.

post.summary: Claim the shoutout-on-X reward
post.description: In the default `oembed` mode the caller pastes the URL of their post and the backend verifies via X's public oEmbed endpoint that it exists and mentions us. Any given post can be redeemed once across the entire waitlist. When X cannot be reached the claim is accepted as `pending` (HTTP 200, `awarded: false`) and a retry job finishes it — a third-party outage never costs the user the reward.

tweetUrl.description: Required in `oembed` mode; ignored in `honor` mode.

post.summary: Record that the X composer was opened
post.description: Instrumentation for the top of the shoutout funnel, and nothing else — it awards no points and does not move `tasks.shoutout`, which still requires the post to come back through `/waitlist/tasks/shoutout` and verify. Without this the click reached GA4 only, so the drop-off between opening the composer and submitting a link was unmeasurable. The timestamp is written on the FIRST click and never moved, so a re-click cannot migrate a click into a later reporting window. Callers should fire this without awaiting it: a failure here must never stop the composer from opening.

post.summary: Start the download-openhuman task
post.description: Records the intent to download and moves the task to `pending`. It **awards no points** — `awarded` is always false here. The reward is granted only once the desktop app actually opens and calls `POST /waitlist/tasks/download/confirm`, so the client should show a waiting state rather than a checkmark. Returns `downloadUrl` (the tracked hop to navigate to) and `deepLinkUrl` (what that hop tries first, for a client that wants to skip the interstitial).

200.description: Reward state plus the tracked download URL

post.summary: Confirm OpenHuman opened, and award the download reward
post.description:
Called by the desktop app on launch with the per-entry download token it received in the `openhuman://waitlist?token=...` deep link. This is the ONLY place the download points are granted — neither the click nor the tracked redirect awards anything.

Authenticated by that token rather than the browser session: the app never sees `x-waitlist-token`. The token is per-entry, so it can only ever award its own entry.

Idempotent — an app that pings on every launch, or retries a failed request, is paid exactly once. `awarded` is true only on the call that actually granted the points; every later call returns false with the task already `awarded`.

token.description: The per-entry download token from the deep link.

clientVersion.description: Desktop build that opened, recorded for telemetry.

awarded.description: True only on the call that granted the points.

get.summary: Tracked download hop — open the app, or fall back to the download
get.description: Serves a small interstitial that first tries the `openhuman://` deep link and, if nothing takes over within roughly 1.3s, redirects to the platform download. Existing users land in the app; new users land on the installer. Records the click and the detected platform, but **awards no points** — the reward is granted only by `POST /waitlist/tasks/download/confirm`, once the app actually opens. Returns HTML, not JSON — it is opened in a browser tab, not called by an API client.
